questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

Three times this was

X-only be compared to the deepest notes of thunder

Y-shook with the noise, that can 

Z-repeated, and each time the earth
questions.solution:
The sentence that could follow ‘three times this was..’ is either ‘shook with the noice’ or ‘repeated..’. From these two, option Z makes the best fit because if Y is chosen as the second sentence, X or Z cannot follow it grammatically or structurally. Therefore, Z is the 1st sentence. This rules out option 2 and 4. Till now the sentence is ‘Three times this was repeated, and each time the earth…’, which is meaningfully followed by ‘shook’ and not ‘only be compared’. 

This makes ZYX as the best answer.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

The causes and their

X-in the same series 

Y-one order, they stand 

Z-effects belong to the
questions.solution: The use of the phrase ‘causes and their’ is appropriate with ‘effects’ as ‘cause and effect’ is an idiom. This makes option 1 and 4 as the prospective correct answers. This now, the sentence forms as ‘The causes and their effects belong to the..’, which can be meaningfully followed by ‘one order’ and not ‘in the same series’. This makes ZYX as the correct sequence.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

Sunita will bake two dozen cupcakes for the bake sale.

options.text: For the bake sale, two dozen cupcakes will be baked by Sunita.
For the bake sale, two dozen cupcakes is baked by Sunita.
Baking of two dozen cupcakes by Sunita will be done for the bake sale.
Baking of two dozen cupcakes by Sunita is done for the bake sale.

questions.solution:
The sentence given in the question clearly indicates ‘Sunita will bake’, therefore, the passive form of the sentence must also contain the future tense representation. 

From the given options, this criterion is qualified by option 1 and 3. However, option 3 is lengthy, while option 1 conveys the same meaning concisely. 

Therefore, the correct passive statement is: 

**For the bake sale, two dozen cookies will be baked by Sunita. **

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

The magician placed the ball (1)/ underneath of his hat and (2)/ made a mystic sign above it. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution: The error is in the 2nd phrase, where ‘underneath of’ is incorrect phrase. The word ‘underneath’ is used to represent an act of hiding something under something else, and its usage is independent. The correct sentence is : The magician placed the ball underneath his hat and made a mystic sign above it.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

My mother said to my father, "I am very busy now."

options.text: My mother told my father that I am very busy now.
My mother told my father that she is very busy.
My mother told my father that she was very busy then.
My mother told my father that I was very busy now.

questions.solution:
As given in the question, mother mentions being busy ‘now’, which must be converted to ‘then’ according to the rule of direct-indirect conversion. 

This rules out option 1 and 4. 

Further, the use of ‘I am very busy’ with ‘now’ does not show any conversion. 

The correct answer is: 

**My mother told my father that she was very busy then.**

questions.question: painters __________ technical knowledge to paint
questions.solution: Clearly, the word ‘painters’ is in the plural form. Therefore, ‘has’ cannot be used. ‘Painters has had’ is also incorrect for the same reason. ‘Painters to have technical knowledge to paint’ makes an incomplete statement. We use ‘have’ with plural form of a noun, therefore, making option 3 as the correct choice.

questions.question: This was enough ___________ the book store-owner-turned librarian
questions.solution: The use of ‘to assess its valuable content’ given in the second part of the sentence contains the hint. This supports the fact that it too much for the owner to assess its valuable contents. Therefore, the word ‘for’ makes the most appropriate option.

questions.question: The grand library ___________ the palace is a cache of knowledge.
questions.solution: The sentence clearly shows that two locations have been connected. Therefore, we need to select a word that connects the two location, i.e. grand library and palace. The use of ‘to’ and ‘off’, therefore, do not fit. The grand library from the palace is also incorrect, because the grand library doesn’t come out of the palace. The use of the word ‘at’ makes the best fit and gives the sentence as: *The grand library at the palace is a cache of knowledge.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Canonical
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Unorthodox**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"canonical"** means something that is recognized or accepted as being accurate and authoritative. (मानक)

 
 
• **Example: **The book is considered **canonical **within the literary community.
 
 
 
• **"Unorthodox" **refers to something that does not conform to traditional or accepted standards or beliefs. (अपरंपरागत)
 
 
• **Example: **His **unorthodox **methods in teaching have proven to be very effective.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'canonical' **is **'unorthodox'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Approved **(स्वीकृत): Officially agreed or accepted as satisfactory.

 
 
• **Example:** The committee **approved **the new policy after much deliberation.
 
 
 
• **Official **(आधिकारिक): Relating to an authority or public body and its duties, actions, and responsibilities.
 
 
• **Example: **The **official **statement was released by the government.
 
 
 
• **Sanctioned** (अनुमोदित): Given official permission or approval.
 
 
• **Example:** The project was **sanctioned **by the board of directors.

questions.solution: Disdain represents a feeling that someone or something is not worthy of respect. ‘Antipathy’ represents lack of respect, which is the synonym of disdain, so rejected. ‘Admiration’ is the act of appreciation, which is the exact opposite, making it the correct answer. ‘Derision’ means mockery and ‘scorn’ means an expression of dislike towards something, which again makes the synonym of disdain.

questions.question:

To Astound
questions.solution:

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

As a fitness ___________, Deepti is always preaching to her friends about the importance of working out.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **enthusiast**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct phrase is ‘fitness enthusiast’, therefore, fitting the blank perfectly.
 
• The hint lies in the fact that we need a noun to fill in the sentence, while ‘enthusiastic’ is an adjective.
 
• ‘Enthusiasm’ might be a noun but it does not make any sense with Deepti being a ‘fitness enthusiasm’.
 
• Also, Deepti being a ‘fitness enthusiastically’ also gives no meaning to the sentence.
 
• Hence, 'enthusiast' is the correct answer.

​The corrected form of the sentence is: *As a fitness **enthusiast**__, Deepti is always preaching to her friends about the importance of working out.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Enthusiasm:** Enthusiasm refers to a strong and eager interest or excitement about something. (उत्साह)
 
• **Enthusiast: **An enthusiast is a person who has a strong and passionate interest in a particular activity, subject, or hobby. (प्रशंसक)
 
• **Enthusiastic: **Enthusiastic is an adjective used to describe someone who shows great excitement, interest, or eagerness about something. (उत्साही)
 
• **Enthusiastically: **Enthusiastically is an adverb that describes an action performed with great enthusiasm or excitement. (उत्साहपूर्वक)
